newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 2.9 pct, politic tension fades.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 2.9 pct, politic tension fades.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged in late buying on Thursday as week-long political concerns over the fate of the Islamist-led coalition government eased, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed 42 points, or 2.94 percent higher at 1,469. It had lost 6.85 percent in the past five days since the market opened last Thursday after a 6-1/2 day holiday.
Daily trade volume rose to 11.59 trillion lira ($85.5 million) from 9.95 trillion ($73.6 million) on Wednesday.
Brokers said the index still faced resistance at the 1,470 level which could prompt profit-taking on Friday after today's sharp rise.

"Today's sudden rise was not so healthy because of weak volume. If political uncertainty disappears completely, then there will be more liquidity influx," said Ali Incekara from Alternatif securities.

Deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller said her conservative True Path Party (DYP) would not abandon its Islamist coalition partners despite a row with the military and the weekend resignation of two DYP ministers over the rise of Islamist activity.
Turkish opposition plans to form a secularist alliance against Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan faltered earlier this week.

Erbakan challenged his critics to early elections on Tuesday after coming under heavy fire from secularist centres, led by the powerful army, for his reluctance to implement measures recommended by the army to fight rising Islamist activism.
